title: 0/1 knapsack
summary: Fill a table of the best value for each number of items and each capacity: leave the item, or take it if it fits.
note: Item i has weight weights[i] and value values[i]; each item is taken whole or not at all.

panels.label: dp[i][c]: best value from the first i items with capacity c

marks.label: take it: dp[i-1][c-w]
marks.when: row == i - 1 and col == c - w and w <= c

narration.text: Build the table one row at a time, every cell starting at zero.
dp[i][c] will be the best value from the first i items with capacity c. With no items, every cell is {dp[0][0]}.
Item {i} is done for every capacity.
Leaving item {i} out, the best is the cell above: {dp[i][c]}.
It fits, and taking it gives {dp[i - 1][c - w] + v}, more than {dp[i][c]}: take it.
It doesn't fit: it weighs {w}, but the capacity is {c}.
Taking it would give {dp[i - 1][c - w] + v}, no better than {dp[i][c]}: leave it.
The best with capacity {c} is now {dp[i][c]}.
The most value that fits in capacity {capacity} is {dp[n][capacity]}.
